notes: ACCESS: robots.txt (https://www.theone.com/robots.txt) has no Claude/anthropic-specific disallow and no blanket User-agent:*/Disallow:/ - tier (a) HTTP fetch permitted, and no anti-bot block was hit at any tier. TREE METHOD: tier (a) curl_cffi (impersonate chrome124) fetch of homepage HTML gave the full static mega-menu (all category slugs incl. 'New' and 'Sale' cross-section duplicates) and https://www.theone.com/sitemap.xml (1407 URLs, 208 /category/ URLs) was cross-checked with a keyword sweep (storage/organiser/basket/box/linen/rug/cushion/towel/curtain/blanket/throw/duvet/pillow/bedding/tapestry/crate/bin/shelv/rack/wardrobe/closet) - no category slugs existed outside the mega-menu set, confirming the tree was complete from tier (a) alone. QTY METHOD: the site (Vue/Nuxt SSR on the Kartmax platform) renders '#km-plp-count' / '#km-product-count' as a placeholder '- 0 Choices' in the raw HTML and only fills the true count client-side via a hashed fast-search API call after hydration (verified: reverse-engineered docket.kartmax.in/.../product-listing/index.js, the API URL uses a per-request client-generated hash so it can't be called deterministically from tier (a)) - escalated to tier (b) Playwright (headless chromium, networkidle + 2-2.5s settle) to read the rendered '#km-plp-count span' text on every leaf page; H1 and canonical link were also captured on each page as evidence and matched the requested slug on every leaf recorded. Never used tier (c). EXCLUDED - Textile: 'Napkin Rings' (9, hardware/tableware accessory not fabric, analogous to curtain-ring hardware exclusion); 'Wall Prints' (66) and 'Wall Décor' (10, contains wall shelves/wall decorations not textile products - Wall Decor category is out of scope for this task); 'New'/'Sale' sections are filtered cross-cuts of the same catalog (duplicate slugs of every category below), not distinct category pages, so excluded entirely to avoid duplicate rows over the same products. EXCLUDED - Storage: 'Living Room Storage' subcategories (Cabinets & Display Units qty2, Bookcases & Shelving qty0, TV & Media Units qty3) and 'Dining Room Storage' subcategories (Buffets & Sideboards qty0, Serving Trolleys qty10) were inspected via product-link text scraping on the rendered page - all contain genuine furniture pieces (display cabinets, TV units, bookcases, sideboards, dining serving trolleys), matching the Furniture-boundary exclusion in storage.md SS16/20/21 even though the site labels the parent node 'Storage'; these are presumed already captured in the validated Furniture.xlsx. 'Bath Accessories' (31), 'Home Office Accessories' (13/151 links), 'Bedroom Accessories' (16) and 'Coat Stands & Hooks' (9) were each spot-checked by scraping product titles: all are mixed general-accessory grab-bags (toilet paper holders, towel trees, bookends, water fountains, ring holders/jewellery stands, coat racks, door stoppers) with only a minority of genuinely storage-purpose items (e.g. a couple of 'storage box'/'jewellery organiser' SKUs inside 'Bedroom Accessories'); since the website's own hierarchy names these as general 'Accessories' (not Storage) and the page-level qty would misrepresent a mixed listing as pure storage, none were recorded as Storage rows per storage.md SS3/SS42 ambiguity handling - primary purpose of the node as a whole is not storage. Net result: this company has a real Textile tree but no genuine dedicated Storage category, so storage_rows is empty (valid NO_CATEGORY outcome per storage.md SS41).
